Step 1 — Install Quarto
Go to https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/ and download the installer for your OS. Takes about 2 minutes. No configuration needed.

Step 2 — Install Python packages
Open your terminal and run:
pip install plotly pandas jupyter nbformat

Step 3 — Set up the project
Copy the entire quarto-oda-site/ folder to wherever you keep projects.
Your folder should look like:
quarto-oda-site/
  _quarto.yml       ← site configuration
  styles.css        ← dark theme
  index.qmd         ← homepage
  oda-trends.qmd    ← first post
  oda-deep-dive.qmd ← second post (add later)

Step 4 — Preview locally
In your terminal, navigate to the folder and run:
cd quarto-oda-site
quarto preview
This opens the site in your browser at http://localhost:4200 Hot-reloads as you edit files. Ctrl+C to stop.

Step 5 — Create a GitHub repository

Go to github.com and sign in (or create a free account)
Click “New repository”
Name it data-stories (or anything you like)
Set it to Public
Click “Create repository”

Step 6 — Publish to GitHub Pages
In your terminal (inside the project folder), run:
quarto publish gh-pages
Quarto will: - Ask you to authenticate with GitHub (opens browser) - Render all your .qmd files to HTML - Push the output to a gh-pages branch - Print the live URL (e.g. https://yourusername.github.io/data-stories)
That’s it. Every time you update a post, run quarto publish gh-pages again.

Step 7 — Link from WordPress
Now that your site has a real URL, you can link to individual posts from WordPress using normal text links — no iframes or scripts needed.
Or add a “Data Stories” page in WordPress that links out to the Quarto site.

Adding new posts

Create a new file like my-new-post.qmd in the project folder
Add it to the navbar in _quarto.yml if you want it in the menu
Run quarto publish gh-pages

Editing existing posts
Just edit the .qmd file and re-publish. Quarto only re-renders changed files (controlled by freeze: auto in _quarto.yml).

Useful Quarto reference

Full docs: https://quarto.org/docs/websites/
Plotly in Quarto: https://quarto.org/docs/interactive/widgets/plotly.html
Theming: https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-themes.html
